vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the swapTokens function. When ETH is sent to marketingAddress via .transfer(), a malicious contract at that address can re-enter with 2300 gas. The marketingAccumulator is only reset to 0 after the external call. During reentrancy, the attacker could potentially manipulate fee calculations or bypass checks. Additionally, the _bypassAmount feature allows fee-free transfers if amount equals _bypassAmount. If _bypassAmount is set to a reasonable value (not total supply), an attacker could use reentrancy to transfer tokens without fees.
attack_strategy: 1. Become the marketing address (requires owner privilege or exploit). 2. Set _bypassAmount to a reasonable value (requires owner). 3. Trigger swapAndLiquify to cause ETH transfer to our malicious contract. 4. During the .transfer() call, re-enter and call transfer with amount == _bypassAmount to bypass fees. 5. Transfer tokens fee-free during the reentrant call.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy malicious contract with receive() function that re-enters token contract. 2. Get owner to set marketingAddress to our contract. 3. Get owner to set _bypassAmount to a reasonable value. 4. Acquire tokens and transfer some to token contract to build up marketingAccumulator. 5. Sell tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify. 6. During ETH transfer, malicious contract re-enters and transfers tokens with amount == _bypassAmount to bypass fees.
